newsitem.title: UK: Brent offered higher as sellers seek U.S interest.
newsitem.headline: Brent offered higher as sellers seek U.S interest.

text.p: North Sea crude sellers angled for higher prices for first-half August cargoes on Thursday and tested the trans-atlantic market for buyers, traders said.
A Brent loading August 6-8 was on offer at August Brent plus 20 cents, five cents more than was paid on Wednesday, though no buyers were yet ready to pay such a high price.
"There is no-one willing to pay that number so far, the market (for dated Brent) is +10/20," said a trader.
While Brent was pushed up, partly by paper positions held by some majors, and other North Sea crudes were offered at strong numbers, cash crude markets were a touch weaker.
Sept/Oct traded at -5 cents, Aug/Sept at +16 cts and contracts for differences for next week (July 28-01) slipped a couple of cents to quote at +0.06/+0.09.
Several Statfjord cargoes were offered at +40 cents, as sellers tried to profit from the continued absence of Iraqi barrels and the tightness of the European crude market.
"We're in a little standstill at the moment," said one trader, with buyers caught between their need to meet requirements and their reluctance to pay big numbers.
High Brent pushed up cargoes shown into the U.S. Gulf where some six companies fished for trans-atlantic opportunities.

Brent was offered at parity to September WTI for September 5-10 delivery, with later arrivals offered at a 5-15 cent discount. Although the arbitrage seemed tight, with the September Brent/WTI around $1.25 a barrel, sellers appeared to have little to lose with the market so high.
"The real trans-atlantic market is not transparent to outsiders," said one player. "There is uncertainty as to what game is being played and some market manipulation."
Prospective Brent buyers in the U.S. were cool to the offers so far but little alternative light, sweet crude was seen available in the early September timeframe.
